Stop letting noisy static analysis scanners flood your backlog with endless false positives. 🛑 

Blitz Strike bridges the gap between modern AI agent frameworks and offensive security by wrapping a complete penetration-testing methodology into a universal Model Context Protocol server.

Traditional automated security testing usually fails in two ways: it relies on noisy pattern-matching that creates false positives, or it produces unverified findings that waste hours of engineering time. Blitz Strike solves this by structuring engagements into a deterministic three-tier pipeline: reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping (BLITZ), static data-flow tracing (EAGLE-EYE), and live validation (STRIKE). 

By exposing these capabilities as an MCP server, you can plug it directly into AI agents like Claude Code or Cursor to execute deep source-to-sink audits and verify vulnerabilities before reporting them.

Key features include:
⚡ Three-tier security methodology combining BLITZ surface triage, EAGLE-EYE source-to-sink taint analysis, and STRIKE live marker-reflection validation.
🔌 Universal Model Context Protocol integration supporting zero-install configuration across major agent environments via automatic client detection and merging.
📚 Comprehensive built-in knowledge base containing over 130 security tools, 317 tool manuals, and 17 engagement playbooks with automatic on-demand execution.
📊 Enterprise-grade reporting and measurement tools including deterministic CVSS v3.1 calculation, findings deduplication, and coverage matrix evaluation.

Whether you want to run automated pre-commit security audits to catch unauthenticated sinks and injection flaws, or perform rapid attack-surface mapping during internal testing engagements, this gives your AI coding assistant the power to find and verify real vulnerabilities locally before pushing code to production.

Check out the repository and level up your security workflow today:
https://github.com/shinthink/blitzstrike

Bring nostalgic desktop-pet energy to modern web interfaces! 🖥️✨

Remember the joy of having a virtual companion follow your mouse around the screen? Frontend engineers and creative technologists, you can now add that exact playful vibe to your web apps with nilbuild/page-mascot.

The Problem:
Modern web interfaces can often feel a bit sterile. Injecting custom, interactive characters usually requires manually slicing complex sprite sheets and handling tedious coordinate math just to get a character to look at the cursor. 

The Solution:
page-mascot is a lightweight, interactive React component that renders a customizable character capable of tracking the user's cursor across different directional angles and reacting with animations when clicked.

Key Features:
🕹️ Sprite sheet architecture driven by cursor angle tracking with a built-in dead zone for smooth head settling.
🤖 AI agent integration via skills that let you generate custom characters and automatically build aligned sprite sheets using prompts and image generation tools.
♿ Built-in accessibility and performance safeguards, including automatic pointer tracking deactivation for non-fine pointers and click-squash animations respecting prefers-reduced-motion.
🎨 Support for multiple artistic rendering styles like color, ink, sketch, riso, paper, and pixel while maintaining structural alignment.

Use Cases:
🚀 Add an interactive branded mascot to SaaS landing pages or developer docs to skyrocket user engagement.
🛠️ Create personalized avatars or desktop-pet style assistants for personal portfolios and creative web apps.

Ready to give your UI some personality with zero manual sprite-sheet headaches? Check out the repo, generate your custom mascot with AI, and drop it into your project today!

👉 https://github.com/nilbuild/page-mascot

Bring absolute coziness to your macOS workflow by outfitting your desktop windows in hand-picked, knitted yarn borders customized per application. 🧶✨

Let's be honest: default terminal aesthetics and plain window borders can feel a bit sterile for long coding sessions. If you are a macOS power user or developer looking to inject some personality into your local development environment without sacrificing functionality, we found your next favorite utility.

Meet Window Sweaters (saragordic/window-sweaters) -- a macOS menu-bar utility built on top of JankyBorders that overlays decorative, knitted texture borders onto active desktop windows, allowing for extensive aesthetic customization of your workspace. 💻🧣

Here is why developers and designers are loving it:
• Over 37 hand-crafted application colourways and customizable stitch patterns like By App and Zigzag
• Dynamic focus tracking that uses macOS Accessibility APIs to follow active application windows in real time
• Extensible configuration supporting custom PNG yarn charts and simple app-matching rules stored in local configuration files
• Local developer tooling including an automated build script, a catalogue renderer, and benchmarking commands

Beyond just looking incredible on live coding streams, video recordings, and personal productivity setups, it is a brilliant engineering deep-dive. Developers can study its local build scripts, Python automation helpers, and wrapper architecture over system-level window managers like JankyBorders, making it a creative masterclass in leveraging private macOS window APIs and accessibility frameworks.

Ready to give your IDE a winter wardrobe? 

Check out the repo and drop a star to support the creator:
https://github.com/saragordic/window-sweaters
